tasks.title: CLAUDE.md — truth-up the tasks.json enforcement story
tasks.description:
Two corrections to `CLAUDE.md`'s "Agent workflow" section.

1. THE ENFORCEMENT SET IS NOW WRONG. CLAUDE.md says direct `Edit`/`Write` on `tasks.json` is "enforced two ways: the per-agent system prompt explicitly bans it, and the post-task reviewer runs with a directory-scoped allowlist covering only `<dataDir>/reviews/**`". There was an unstated THIRD lock: the reviewer had no Bash at all, so it could not run `cairn task set-status` either. Task #77 removes that lock by granting the reviewer git-inspection subcommands and the reviewed task's test commands.

   Document the actual enforcement set as it now stands: the prompt ban, the directory-scoped write allowlist, and the explicit `permissions.deny` rules on the five mutating `cairn task` subcommands that `cairn init` writes (task #80). Record two facts that are easy to get wrong:
   - Deny rules are NOT enforced under `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, so they do not bind `cairn run` execution agents. They bind the reviewer and planner, which run in normal permission mode. This asymmetry is intended.
   - The deny covers mutating subcommands ONLY. A blanket `Bash(cairn task:*)` would break `cairn task next-id`, which task generation requires; deny beats allow with no exception mechanism.

2. SCOPE THE BAN ITSELF. "Direct `Edit` or `Write` on `tasks.json` is forbidden" currently contradicts `commands/generate-tasks.md:159`, which explicitly instructs the planning session to write `.cairn/tasks.json` using the Write tool. Both are right in intent — the ban targets EXECUTION AGENTS mutating a live task list mid-round, whereas task generation authors the file wholesale between rounds. Add a clause saying so, so the two documents stop contradicting each other.

CRITICAL GUARD — DO NOT MODIFY `cairn.json`. Its `healthCheck` is currently pinned to a throwaway outfile (`bun build --compile src/index.ts --outfile /tmp/cairn-healthcheck`) and is USER-MANAGED for this round. CLAUDE.md documents the REAL value (`bun run build` / `bun build --compile src/index.ts --outfile dist/cairn`) and must continue to. While the round runs, CLAUDE.md and `cairn.json` will legitimately disagree about the health check. That disagreement is EXPECTED and must NOT be "fixed" in either direction. In a previous round exactly this trap caused the pinned value to be committed permanently.
tasks.notes:
# Task #83 — CLAUDE.md: truth-up the tasks.json enforcement story

## What changed

Single file touched: `CLAUDE.md`, one paragraph in the "Agent workflow"
section (was line 88) replaced with a scoped ban sentence + a 3-item
enforcement list + a 2-item "easy to get wrong" list + the closing
`writeTasksFile()` sentence.

### 1. Scoped the ban (part 2 of the task)

Old text: "Direct `Edit` or `Write` on `tasks.json` is **forbidden**." —
flatly contradicted `commands/generate-tasks.md:159`, which tells the
planning session to write `.cairn/tasks.json` with the Write tool.

New text scopes the ban to *execution agents mutating a live task list
mid-round*, and states explicitly that task generation is exempt because it
authors the file wholesale **between** rounds, when no `cairn run` loop is
live and there is no concurrent-mutation race to protect against. The two
documents no longer contradict each other.

### 2. Corrected the enforcement set from two to three (part 1)

Old text claimed enforcement was "two ways" (prompt ban + reviews-dir
allowlist). That was already stale, and had an unstated third lock (the
reviewer having no Bash at all) which task #77 removed by granting it git
inspection + the reviewed task's test commands.

Now documented as three:
1. per-agent system prompt ban
2. directory-scoped Edit/Write allowlist (`<dataDir>/reviews/**`) — all the
   existing prose about `GIT_INSPECTION_RULES` / `buildCommandRules` /
   `reviewsDir` derivation preserved verbatim as a sub-bullet, nothing
   dropped
3. **NEW**: `permissions.deny` rules on the five mutating `cairn task`
   subcommands (`start`, `complete`, `set-status`, `add`, `note`) written by
   `cairn init` — pointer to `CAIRN_TASK_DENY_RULES` in
   `src/commands/init.ts:481-487`. Explains *why* it exists: granting the
   reviewer any Bash at all would otherwise hand it `cairn task set-status`,
   i.e. task-state mutation without touching the file.

Plus the two required easy-to-get-wrong facts:
- Deny rules are NOT enforced under `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, so
  they do not bind `cairn run` execution agents; they bind the reviewer and
  planner (normal permission mode). Asymmetry is intended.
- Deny covers mutating subcommands ONLY — a blanket `Bash(cairn task:*)`
  would break `cairn task next-id` (required by task generation); deny beats
  allow with no exception mechanism.

## Verification (facts checked against source, not assumed)

- `src/commands/init.ts:481-487` — `CAIRN_TASK_DENY_RULES` contains exactly
  the five subcommands named: `start`, `complete`, `set-status`, `add`,
  `note`. `next-id` and `show` are absent (reachable).
- `grep -rn "dangerously-skip-permissions" src/` → only
  `src/commands/run.ts:210` (execution agents) and
  `src/commands/summarize.ts:107`. `src/commands/plan.ts` and
  `src/post-task-reviewer.ts` do **not** pass it — confirming the documented
  asymmetry (reviewer + planner run in normal permission mode, and are
  therefore the agents the deny rules actually bind).
- `commands/generate-tasks.md:159` — confirmed it does instruct "write
  `.cairn/tasks.json` directly using the Write tool", i.e. the contradiction
  the task describes was real.

## CRITICAL GUARD honored

`cairn.json` was **not** modified. Confirmed before and after that its
`healthCheck` is still the pinned throwaway outfile
(`bun build --compile src/index.ts --outfile /tmp/cairn-healthcheck`), while
CLAUDE.md continues to document the REAL value (`bun run build` /
`... --outfile dist/cairn`) in both the Development section and the
Conventions section. **That disagreement is expected for the duration of
this self-modifying round and must NOT be "fixed" in either direction** —
see the Pin/unpin section of CLAUDE.md. Neither file's health-check text was
touched by this task.

## Tests

`bun run test` → **881 pass, 0 fail** across 30 files — unchanged from the
881 at the start of this iteration, as expected: this was a documentation-
only change with no source under test. No test was added; CLAUDE.md prose
has no test surface (there is no doc-lint or prose-assertion harness in this
repo, and inventing one was outside this task's declared file scope of
`CLAUDE.md`).

## Nothing left for the next agent

Both corrections are complete. No new tasks filed — nothing unrelated
surfaced.

tasks.title: README.md — document the permission rules init now writes
tasks.description:
Document the new `cairn init` behavior added in task #80.

Add to `README.md` — the Workflow > Initialize section is the natural home, with a cross-reference from Configuration if useful:

1. That `cairn init` offers to write permission rules to `.claude/settings.local.json`, and that the prompt defaults to yes but is skippable.
2. WHAT gets written: read-only git inspection subcommands, allow rules derived from the project's `healthCheck` and `defaultTestCommand`, and deny rules on the five mutating `cairn task` subcommands.
3. WHY: agents that verify a task actually landed — chiefly the post-task reviewer — need to run tests and inspect history. Without these rules a fresh project denies them outright in headless mode.
4. That EXISTING settings are MERGED, not replaced: `permissions.allow` and `permissions.deny` are unioned and every other key is preserved untouched. A user who already has settings from plain `claude` usage will not lose them.
5. That the user should add `.claude/settings.local.json` to their own gitignore — Cairn deliberately does not edit `.gitignore` or global git config, and Claude Code only auto-ignores that file when it writes the file itself.

Keep the existing README structure and table formatting conventions.

CRITICAL GUARD — DO NOT MODIFY `cairn.json`. Its `healthCheck` is pinned to a throwaway outfile and is user-managed for this round. Any disagreement between documentation and `cairn.json`'s current value is EXPECTED — do not reconcile it.
